violatedPolicies.name: CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability added
violatedPolicies.description: Alert on deployments with containers escalating with CAP_SYS_ADMIN
violatedPolicies.remediation: Ensure that the container really needs the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability or use a userspace derivative.

violatedPolicies.name: Container with privilege escalation allowed
violatedPolicies.description: Alerts if a deployment has containers with allowPrivilegeEscalation set to true in its security context.
violatedPolicies.remediation: Verify that privileged escalation is required and cannot be provided with a subset of other controls. Disable privilege escalation by setting allowPrivilegeEscalation to false.

violatedPolicies.name: Docker CIS 5.15: Ensure that the host's process namespace is not shared
violatedPolicies.description: The Process ID (PID) namespace isolates the process ID space, meaning that processes in different PID namespaces can have the same PID. This creates process level isolation between the containers and the host.
violation: Deployment uses the host's process ID namespace
violatedPolicies.remediation: You should not create a deployment with `hostPID: true`

violatedPolicies.name: No CPU request or memory limit specified
violatedPolicies.description: Alert on deployments that have containers without CPU request or memory limit
violation: CPU request set to 0 cores for container 'ai-agent'
Memory limit set to 0 MB for container 'ai-agent'
violatedPolicies.remediation: Specify CPU request and memory limit for your deployment.
